title: `ScriptEditor` focus loss when using `next_script` / `prev_script` shortcuts
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6.1-stable, 4.7-dev 220b0b2f74d8e089481b140c42a42992a76dd6fc

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev (7ba9f75c9) - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 63.11 GiB memory

### Issue description

When using the `next_script` / `prev_script` (`ctrl`+`shift`+`,`/`.`) shortcuts and holding them down, to switch by more than one script, sometimes after letting go the open editor looses focus. This is especially noticeable in script files where the caret is no longer showing and you need to click on the editor before you can change code.

From my testing the focus loss only happens after `ScriptEditor::shortcut_input` is done so it is probably something which happens from a delayed function / update.

### Steps to reproduce

1. open the script editor in any project
2. open at least 2 scripts and/or docs
3. hold one of `ctrl`+`shift`+`,`/`.` until the open tab changed multiple times, then let go
4. repeat 3. until script files no longer show a caret / are no longer editable without clicking on them

> Note: When the focus is lost is not easy to notice as the caret is invisible initially even if the focus is on the editor (This should probably be changed so that when an editor gets focus the blinking should start with the caret being visible) you either need to check that you can change the code or wait until the caret shows up to confirm the focus is not lost, and if so try again until neither works/happens. Also the focus recovers when switching tabs again.
